rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an in situ laser re-melting step during powder bed fusion, whereas the hidden target uses atmosphere-controlled debinding of DLP-printed green bodies followed by solid-state sintering. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (additive manufacturing process modification vs. post-printing thermal treatment atmosphere control).

The hidden target involves DLP printing with specific exposure settings, followed by debinding in oxygen-rich or oxygen-deficient environments and sintering at 800–1100 °C. The processing regimes are entirely different.

The hidden target's mechanism involves carbon retention and reduced gas evolution during oxygen-deficient debinding, which limits cracking and facilitates diffusion and densification. These are different classes of mechanism (re-melting vs. debinding atmosphere effects on carbon/oxygen and diffusion).
